_comment: SESSION 23's FIRST SHALLOW ORDINAL, pinned -- and it pins the OTHER half of the user's doctrine.
The user's own claude_s9_gi8, turn 4, main-phase ordinal FIVE: the fifth decision of the turn,
i.e. right after the plan that assembles the loop, not fifty banking clicks later. Session 23's
fixture list splits the ten reference frames the button fires on into SHALLOW ordinals (5, 5, 8)
and DEEP ones (27-63); the shallow three are the only ones a plan-apply shortcut can reach at
all, because the state it must fire on EXISTS in a single main-phase decision's menu.
Board, read straight out of the recording: Cloud of Faeries + Emiel the Blessed over four lands
-- Kitchen carrying Overgrowth (1+2), Conservatory carrying Wild Growth (1+1), a second
Conservatory already tapped, and Mariposa Military Base as the only colourless AND the only
repeatable draw. `library_top` is the deck minus battlefield/hand, which comes to exactly the
49 the recording records -- so the CONTENTS are exact (four Living Wishes among them, which is
what rule WISH-DRAW's W ingredient reads) while the ORDER is canonical, not the real shuffle.
IT IS OFFERED AND NOT VERIFIED, and that is the assertion -- `combo_off_verify: false`.
The recording agrees: its own ordinal-5 menu carries `combo_off: true, rule WISH-DRAW` with NO
`combo_off_verified`, and the user went on to bank twenty-eight hand-blinks ({G:80} floating)
before the click actually won on turn 4. So this frame is the 'display aggressive, execution
exact' split itself: the arithmetic says a combo off is reachable from this position, and the
trial apply honestly declines to promise it THIS instant. Checked, not assumed -- moving a
Living Wish to the top of the library does not make it verify either (x109, still no kill), so
the refusal is the board's net-1 loop against fifty {C} pips, not the synthetic library order.
What it guards: a change that WITHDREW this offer (the user's 'we simply do not get the Combo
Off button in enough cases') and, equally, a change that made it claim 'wins this turn' here.
